previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of T1-T2 paraplegia, recurrent pneumonias, neurogenic bladder, and restrictive ventilatory defect on home oxygen was admitted with fever, increased secretions, and dyspnea. She had a history of recent hospitalization for pneumonia and septic shock. Imaging showed a right pleural effusion and right lower lobe opacity, concerning for aspiration pneumonia. She was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, but developed leukopenia and thrombocytopenia, prompting a switch from cefepime and vancomycin to ceftaroline. A repeat chest X-ray revealed new mild pulmonary edema, suggesting acute diastolic heart failure. Despite medical recommendations to remain hospitalized, she elected to leave against medical advice. She was discharged home with services on IV antibiotics (ceftaroline and flagyl) via home infusion, oral lasix, and all baseline medications, with instructions to follow up in primary care, pulmonary, and infectious disease clinics.

# SEPTIC SHOCK / STENOTROPHOOMAS BACTEREMIA / PNEUMONIA: She 
presented with dyspnea and was found to have an increased 
respiratory rate and hypotensive with labs showing leukocytosis. 
 CXR was concerning for possible LLL pneumonia.  Influenza DFA 
was negative for influenza.  She was started on 
vancomycin/cefepime for HCAP (___). Oseltamivir and azithromycin 
were also started initially but were discontinued with negative 
influenza and legionella testing.  Her blood culture grew 
Stenotrophomonas and she was started on bactrim.  Surveillance 
cultures were obtained and are no growth but not finalized at 
the time of discharge.  Her sputum grew MRSA and she was 
initially treated with vancomycin although this was later 
stopped as it was sensitive to bactrim.  Her indwelling tunneled 
line was removed.  Her urine grew Klebsiella ESBL although this 
was thought to represent colonization as her urinalysis was more 
bland.  She will complete a 2 week course of bactrim from the 
time the line is removed/first negative culture. 
.
 TOXIC / METABOLIC ENCEPHALOPATHY: She was inattentive and 
lacked proper orientation on exam. This was likely due to  her 
acute medical illness. TSH was within normal limits. Sedating 
medications (trazadone, benzodiazepine) were initially held. Her 
condition improved and she was felt to be at baseline at the 
time of discharge. 
.
# POLYSUBSTANCE ABUSE: Urine toxicology screen was positive for 
cocaine and methadone. There was some concern in the ICU  that 
her visitors were supplying her narcotics. She was initially 
monitored with a 1:1 sitter  and psychiatry as consulted. When 
her mental status improved she admitted to taking methadone at 
home for her chronic pain. This is not a prescribed medication 
and she reported getting it from a friend. She had been 
previously prescribed narcotics by her PCP but was in violation 
of her narcotics contract so this was stopped in ___.  She was 
noted to have increased anxiety and abdominal pain during her 
hospital stay that could be seen in narcotics withdrawal.  We 
discussed that she consider a substance abuse treatment program 
to wean her off narcotics and so that a better treatment plan 
could be developed.  Social work met with her to discuss 
resources. She was not interested at this time. 
.
# CHRONIC NEUROPATHIC PAIN: She has a history of spinal cord 
injury and chronic neuropathic pain. She was continued on her 
home pain control regimen of gabapentin, baclofen, lidocaine 
patch and tylenol.  The patient ask her ICU and floor providers 
for narcotics.  She did not receive narcotics during the 
hospitalization as her pain was chronic and there was no plan in 
place to continue narcotics as an outpatient.  She will follow 
up with ___ pain clinic and has an appointment within one week

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  CHEST, FRONTAL AND LATERAL VIEWS.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Shortness of breath upon awaking today.

___.

FINDINGS:  Right-sided central venous catheter which terminates at the
cavoatrial junction.  There is persistent right base opacity and likely
atelectasis/scarring in the left lower lung.  Interstitial edema is again seen
stable to possibly minimally improved.  The right costophrenic angle is not
fully included on the frontal image and the right pleural effusion is
difficult to entirely exclude.  Cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are
stable.  Partially imaged is hardware in the left humerus.

HISTORY:  Paraplegia with worsening hypoxia.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images were taken through the chest after
the administration of intravenous contrast material.  Coronal and sagittal as
well as maximum intensity projection oblique reformats were examined.

DLP:  722.80 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Chest CT ___.

FINDINGS:

The thyroid is unremarkable.  The airways are patent to the subsegmental
level.  Previously seen ground glass opacities are improved on the current
study.  There has been interval slight progression of the consolidation at the
left lower lobe.  An area of rounded atelectasis is also again seen at the
left lung base, stable since the prior study. Again seen is chronic
consolidation/atelectasis at the right lung base with a chronic right pleural
effusion.  There is also a small left pleural effusion.  

The aorta and pulmonary arteries are well opacified.  There is no pulmonary
embolism in the main, right, left, or segmental pulmonary arteries.  The main
pulmonary artery is stable in size.

Again seen is mediastinal lymphadenopathy, which is also stable since prior
study.  There is slight interval enlargement of a right upper paratracheal
lymph node, now measuring 1.2 cm on the current study.

No suspicious lesion is present in the visualized osseous structures. 
Multiple bilateral healed rib fractures are again noted.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  No pulmonary embolism.  

2.  Slight interval progression of the left lower lobe opacities which may
represent developing infection.  

3.  Stable chronic collapse of the right lower lobe with associated pleural
effusion.

HISTORY:  Increased respiratory distress.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

Again seen is a right-sided central venous catheter which terminates in the
right atrium.  The heart is severely enlarged.  There is pulmonary vascular
redistribution.  There are bilateral lower lobe infiltrates and small
bilateral pleural effusions.  There are patchy areas of alveolar opacity in
the right mid and upper lung.

IMPRESSION:

Worsened CHF.  An infectious infiltrate, particularly on the right cannot be
exclude.

INDICATION:  Paraplegia, recurrent pneumonias/UTI requiring frequent IV
antibiotics with tunneled central venous line, admitted with bacteremia,
please remove line, do not replace with another line.

PHYSICIAN:  ___, M.D., fellow, performed the procedure.

MEDICATIONS:  Small quantity of 2% lidocaine locally.

PROCEDURES:  Removal of tunneled central line.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  The patient was positioned supine.  The area was prepped
and draped in sterile fashion.  A timeout was performed.  Small amount of
lidocaine was applied locally.  With minor blunt dissection, the tunneled
catheter was removed under sterile technique.  The tip was sent for culture. 
There was good hemostasis.  A dressing was applied.  There were no
complications.

SPECIMEN:  Catheter tip culture.

CONCLUSION:  Uncomplicated removal of a tunneled central venous catheter.

INDICATION:  ___ female with pneumonia and bacteremia who presents for
evaluation of nausea and abdominal pain.  Question obstruction.

COMPARISONS:  Chest radiograph from ___ and ___.  Chest
CT from ___.

FINDINGS:  

CHEST: There appears to be interval removal of the right-sided central
catheter.  Again seen is severe cardiomegaly, stable compared to the prior
exam.  There has been interval improvement in the pulmonary edema.  There are
small bilateral pleural effusions.  There has been slight interval increase in
the left lower lobe infiltrate.  The right lower lobe infiltrate is stable. 
The cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are stable.  Partially imaged is
hardware in the left humerus.

ABDOMEN: Evaluation of the abdomen is severely limited by significant
overlying soft tissue.  No definite distended loops of bowel are seen.  There
are no air-fluid levels. No definite pneumatosis or free air is identified. 
An IVC filter is seen at the level of L4-5.

IMPRESSION:

Limited evaluation of the abdomen given significant overlying soft tissue,
however, no distended loops of bowel are seen.  No definite evidence of
obstruction.

A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.
